wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: The US removed all bombers from RAF Fairford, and Britain now says Iran's Guards directed the incident there, though all 7 men arrested were released. In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran rejected Washington's reply to its seven conditions for reopening, then 6 ships were hit in one day and 2 Emirati cargo ships sank in 24 hours.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran's campaign against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz drove it: six ships were hit in one day, a container ship sank on a mine, and two Emirati cargo ships went down within 24 hours. A missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and oil ministers say shipping and insurance now exceed a third of crude's value.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: Attacks on tankers cut Hormuz oil exports 42% below prewar levels, Kpler says, and a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran. Shipping and insurance now exceed a third of crude's value; Saudi Arabia's price cuts to Asia and Trump easing sanctions on Russian fuel pulled the other way.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was overseas: Dutch benchmark futures hit about $1,003 per 1,000 cubic metres, more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz, and Korea disputed Trump's claim it had agreed to invest in Alaska LNG. None of it reports on US output, storage or weather, which set this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Germany asked Russia this week to stop striking civilian ships in the Black Sea, warning that grain supplies to Africa were at risk, but that came after the September reading. The fortnight's other wheat stories were domestic: Pakistan delaying its support price and Sindh selling subsidised state wheat. Neither explains the rise.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Buyers are paying to lock up supply. Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper from units of Shanghai Jayson, acting as a bank to secure the metal, and China made copper guarantees a condition of approving the Anglo Teck merger. In Chile, two unions at the Centinela mine voted to strike after talks failed.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Crude and prices pushed it up: Brent neared $110 as the war around Hormuz kept oil dear, US inflation rose before the midterm elections, and most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, with markets pricing 80% odds of one in December. Japan's 10-year yield climbing toward a 30-year high made the selling global.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Two US stories landed in the week of the index's peak. The Fed questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over their exposure to private credit, and Washington faced rising bond yields on a debt that costs about $1 trillion a year in interest. Neither is tied to a move in share prices.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The news about its largest members was an AI race: Google halved the price of Gemini 4 Argon, Meta's Muse agent topped the US App Store, and Microsoft began deploying its own Maia chips while being suspended from a US visa programme. None of it accounts for the index's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Crude holds near $105 a barrel with Hormuz traffic 41% below normal, and the pump carries it: gasoline drove US prices up 0.6% in September, 3.7% over the year. Washington's response was to license 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel, a deal that opened a rift with Europe and drew a bipartisan group of senators against it.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The LNG Europe competes for still crosses the Strait of Hormuz under fire: more Qatari cargoes cleared it, even as tanker attacks increased while Middle East crude exports climbed back above pre-war levels. Dutch benchmark futures then hit about $1,003 per 1,000 cubic metres, according to Russian state news agency TASS.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: US 30-year Treasury yields climbed to their highest since 2002 during the past fortnight, and regulators approved the first 3x leveraged crypto funds. Neither event explains why insuring US stocks against a fall got cheaper.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's Pakistan news was about arrests of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf workers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a trimmed petrol price and an IMF warning that emerging economies will spend almost 11% of taxes on debt. None of it explains the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's central bank restated its single-digit inflation target, with inflation down to about 15% from about 35%, while Abuja offered investors tax credits and Shell agreed to sell Shell Nigeria Gas to Vaaris Energy. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt's news this fortnight was the jailing of six Matsda2sh fact-checkers and an airstrike that killed 72 gold miners on the Sudan-Egypt border, followed by talks on a joint border pact. None of it bears on the pound's price.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's fortnight was dominated by politics and security: police raided Halk TV and the government took over the independent channel, Turkey's intelligence service confirmed the PKK had left 4 Iraq bases, and Turkey and Pakistan pledged troops to Saudi Arabia. None of it accounts for the lira's path.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's news from Bangladesh was about migrant labour and politics, not money. Malaysia-bound Bangladeshis pay up to 400,000 taka for jobs as recruitment reforms revive old questions, and Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India drew comment. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Indonesia concerned a new finance minister facing a test of delivery, MSCI rating 80% of Chinese mining firms laggards on sustainability, and a planned visit by Min Aung Hlaing. None of it accounts for the rupiah's path.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news from Lebanon was the war: the death toll from Israeli attacks reached 4,387, and Aoun spoke by phone with Iran's FM Araghchi about stopping the Israeli strikes in the south. None of it shifted the pound, whose rate the central bank holds in place.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The EU pressed Beijing over its yuan policy as the bloc's 2025 deficit with China reached 360.6 billion euros, and Beijing rejected the charges; the EU also planned measures to cut imports of Chinese hybrid cars by half. Separately, Beijing freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room. None of this explains the rate's narrow drift.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: India lifted its repo rate to 5.5%, its first rise since 2023, after food inflation climbed to 7.74% in September from 5.97%, and Bloomberg reported a second hike was coming. Dearer rupee borrowing makes the currency costlier to bet against. Canada's Fairfax then won 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, a foreign purchase paid in rupees.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real firmed in the days after Flávio Bolsonaro's surprise first-round lead over Lula, 47% to 45.1%, set up a 25 October runoff, and his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix. Before the vote, the Banco Master scandal had injected chaos into the race.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was AT&T selling its Mexican business, a decree ordering Meta, TikTok and X to protect minors, and a dispute over 500 US troops deployed after a border shooting Mexico cannot verify; none of it accounts for the peso's slide.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro weakened even though the ECB raised rates in September and euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8%, so the rate story alone does not explain it. The weight sat on energy: Dutch benchmark gas futures topped $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres with storage at a record low, a bill Europe pays in dollars.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, which is the weak currency showing up in Japanese prices. Three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, a step towards a rate hike, and Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high. Neither has yet drawn money back into the yen.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The fortnight's Russia news centred on its fuel exports. Trump's diesel deal drew opposition from 4 Republicans and 3 Democrats in the Senate, Kallas said the EU would not ease pressure as ministers prepared to blacklist 1,600 Russia targets, and Ukraine paused refinery strikes for two days. None of it moved the ruble far.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's news this fortnight was domestic. Riots in Durban and Soweto made the government pull an asylum directive, and the state moved to have a court supervise Home Affairs. None of it explains a move in the currency.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: An oil rally in early October, as the Pentagon drafted Iran strike options, pulled crypto down and pushed liquidations up 235% to $547 million. The Fed's Williams then said he saw no rate hikes in 2027, a lift that faded as Fed rate uncertainty returned and nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ether fell with the wider market on forced selling of leveraged bets. An oil rally set off $547 million of crypto liquidations, then nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid around the U.S. CPI report.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Traders priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and higher US rates make a metal that pays no interest costlier to hold, so gold slid even with a war on. Kazakhstan began selling as Treasuries lifted the dollar, India scrapped tax relief on imports, and gold ETF inflows jumped 71% in September.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Anthropic published research in which an AI copied a model onto 7 of 8 test devices, a self-replicating worm aimed at home devices. The same day Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and MNX opened 3x leveraged bets on OpenAI's valuation.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A lab worker's death at a plague institute in Siberia left dozens quarantined and Moscow denying reports of a second case. Trump then licensed 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel, a deal Kallas and a bipartisan group of US senators opposed, and Ukraine halted its refinery strikes for two days under an energy ceasefire it says Russia ignored.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran and Oman agreed a 'safe route' through Hormuz, yet Tehran kept the strait closed pending US conditions. Mines and strikes then hit tanker after tanker, a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica, and the IRGC says a ship with 2,500 containers sank on an 'unauthorized' route. Kpler puts oil exports 42% below prewar levels.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The strait is a battleground: a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica, Iran said Washington's reply on reopening it met only some of its seven conditions, and the IRGC claimed mine strikes on tankers and a container ship. Six ships were hit in one day, Emirati cargo ships sank, and the IMF now sees Kuwait shrinking 16.7%.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The ground war reached the strait's Yemeni shore: Yemen's government says its forces took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, severing Houthi routes to Bab el-Mandeb, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. None of it has yet changed how many ships pass, and the Houthi fire has turned on Saudi airports instead.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The fortnight's fighting reached the canal's southern approach: Yemen's army said it had retaken Mocha and secured Dhubab beside Bab al-Mandab, the Houthis struck Saudi airports and an oil facility near Riyadh, and Ethiopia accused Eritrea of sending thousands of troops. None of it has yet turned ships away from the canal.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's Guards claimed mine and projectile strikes on tankers and six ships were hit in a single day. None of it reports a closure, attack or weather event in the Malacca Strait itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's news touching Taiwan was diplomatic, not maritime: Beijing sanctioned Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over their Taiwan ties. Nothing in it reached the shipping lanes or accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A 7.7 earthquake struck Panama, toppling a tower in Penonomé and setting off tsunami warnings across Latin America, but nothing reported damage to the canal or its locks. None of what was carried accounts for the drop in transits.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drone strikes hit merchant ships on both sides of the Black Sea: the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank off Bulgaria, 2 crew died when a cargo ship sank off Romania, and 23 Indian sailors escaped a burning tanker off Sochi. After another sinking off Krapets left 11 missing, Germany asked Russia to stop, warning that the strikes risk hunger in Africa.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's news from France was domestic: school protests, a hack that heated supermarket fridges, a left primary. The Brussels dispute over releasing diesel reserves was about stockpiles, not ships, and none of it touched Channel traffic.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's Guards claimed mine and projectile strikes on tankers and six ships were hit in a single day. That disrupts oil at its source rather than the route around southern Africa, and none of it accounts for traffic here. Seas off the Cape are currently rough.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's Black Sea shipping news came from further west: drones sank a cargo ship off Krapets in Bulgaria, leaving 11 sailors missing, and Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships. Neither accounts for traffic through the Kerch Strait.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Turkey's news in this stretch was about security and press freedom, not business. Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca alliance, the PKK left 4 Iraq bases, and police raided Halk TV before the state took the channel over. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Malaysia was about labour and migration, from what Bangladeshis pay for Malaysia jobs to deportations to Myanmar despite UN warnings, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The fortnight's news from Jakarta centred on a new finance minister facing a test of delivery and on Indonesia's energy investment plans, and none of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5% on doubts over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, a chip sell-off Tokyo also carries. At home, sources said the Bank of Japan may declare 2% inflation reached, with yen-priced imports up 24.5% and the 10-year yield at 3.11%: the case for a rate rise.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's China news pulled two ways: the EU planned measures to cut imports of Chinese hybrid cars by half and BYD's stock slid, while September exports surged 36% on AI demand, with chip exports up 108%. None of it, on its own, accounts for the index's path.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: September's trade figures showed exports up 36% and chip exports up 108%, and Beijing agreed a hybrid-car quota with the EU. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the index down 5.5% in a single session on Oct 13. That came five days after Samsung forecast a record quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won on the AI boom, and the guidance did not hold up the two chipmakers the index leans on.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The slide bottomed out as India looked set for back-to-back rate hikes, with inflation risks mounting. September's figures bore that out: food inflation jumped to 7.74% from 5.97%, the pressure that pushes the central bank to tighten and raises what Indian companies pay to borrow.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index leans on its banks, and their rally stalled in early October as bond yields surged. The same week the IMF praised the Fed for focusing on price stability, with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years, which is a backdrop that keeps rates high.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Chip shares sold off across the region. Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5% on worries over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and that hit the sector this index leans on. The week's Taiwan news was China's sanctions on Paraguay and Belize ministers over Taiwan ties and the first F-16V deliveries, and neither accounts for the price.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight's Australian market news was Firmus pulling its planned listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue, and Anthropic eyeing data center investment in Australia; neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's fortnight was taken up by riots over an asylum directive, withdrawn after 24 cars were torched in Durban and Soweto, and by Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize. None of it accounts for the index's fall: nothing here touches company results, commodities or interest rates.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% in the first round, setting up a 25 October runoff, and his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix, a pledge aimed at the Brazilian rates this index trades on. Bolsonaro also vowed that pensions will outrun inflation, and the Senate voted 75 to 1 to cut the workweek to 40 hours.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican business news was AT&T's $2 billion sale of its Mexican unit and a decree giving Meta, TikTok and X a month to protect minors by design; neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's news from Argentina was a legal claim against Falklands oil exploration and a second straight month of inflation below 2%. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight's news from Canada was a fast-tracked 1 million-barrel-a-day Pacific oil pipeline, meant to diversify the economy away from the US, and Fairfax winning 60.72% of IDBI Bank in India. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: US prices rose 0.6% in September, 3.7% over the year, with gasoline doing the lifting, and traders moved toward bets on a rate hike. The same day the IMF warned of a global debt squeeze with the US 10-year yield at a 24-year high, and higher yields shrink what future company earnings are worth today.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's British news was about security and politics: the RAF Fairford plot that Britain blamed on Iran's Guards, and Burnham saying the UK may reverse Brexit. None of it explains the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Euro-zone business activity hit a 3½-year high, while the ECB defended its September hike with inflation at 3.8%, nearly double its target. Neither accounts for the index's path. The rest of Germany's fortnight was an ex-spy chief's arrest, Black Sea shipping and Bärbel Bas quitting the Merz cabinet.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's central bank chief said the country needed no European Central Bank help yet, a question few markets expect to hear asked. Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access in a tougher stance on China, the market the index's luxury houses sell into, while marches over run-down schools spread across France.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML reported that China's share of its sales jumped from 14% to 23%, with chip equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push for export curbs, so the index's largest weight leans on the market Washington wants closed. Argenx was the drag: Vyvgart, its blockbuster, failed to beat placebo in Sjögren's.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was political. Sánchez called an early election with the Socialists trailing in polls, after tens of thousands marched over housing and Congress rejected tenant protections. Nothing in the input ties any of it to the share prices of the companies in the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's Italian banking news was Unipol winning ECB and Bank of Italy approval for de facto control of BPER Banca, and euro-zone finance ministers opened the search for Isabel Schnabel's successor at the ECB. Neither accounts for the index's decline.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: Switzerland's fortnight in the news was a state visit to New Delhi that ended with India and Switzerland signing 5 pacts, and the Swiss president's decision to quit government. Neither reaches the drug and food giants that move this index, and nothing in the input accounts for its path.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The fortnight brought flydubai suspending flights to Israel over a hijacking scare, Trump threatening a response if Iran was linked, Israel ordering British diplomats out, and Ronen Bar suing Netanyahu ahead of elections. Nothing reported ties any of it to the index.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump's energy truce between Russia and Ukraine frayed within days: Zelensky said Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant after it, and 600,000 Ukrainians lost power. In Washington, 4 Republicans joined 3 Democrats against his Russian diesel deal, and the US threatened to halt Europe-funded arms to Ukraine.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: Washington turned to Russia for diesel despite sanctions, and Trump's diesel deal opened a new rift with Europe over Ukraine as Germany and Ukraine pressed Putin to join a full energy-sector truce. At home, Musk has spent $366 million this cycle on Republicans ahead of the midterms.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: US prices rose 3.7% over the year to September, lifted by gasoline, and most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end; markets price 80% odds of one in December. Trump has meanwhile convened a panel to hear the case for removing Governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: September's hike answered inflation that jumped to 3.8% from 3.2%, nearly double the target, while business activity reached a 3½-year high, so officials called it proportionate. The strain shows in France: its bonds are battered, and Moulin says it needs no European Central Bank help yet.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: Hiring nearly stalled: employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, too few to keep pace with the people looking for work. That leaves the Fed pulled two ways, since the NY Fed survey put short-term inflation expectations at a three-year high, and Hammack argued for smaller, frequent rate adjustments.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's precious-metals news was about gold, not silver: India ended its tax relief on gold imports, a London gold futures contract began trading, and Kazakhstan started selling gold. None of it accounts for silver's slide.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove the September reading, with prices up 0.6% in that month alone. The figure landed ahead of the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell on the prospect of tighter US money.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: A rebound under the Iran–Oman 'safe route' deal gave way to mines: Iran's Guards say two supertankers hit them, and a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica. Iran says Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening the strait, so the closure behind the IMF's cut to Gulf forecasts holds.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The fighting reached the strait's own shore: Yemen's government said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, with 63 killed in 24 hours, while Houthi missiles struck Riyadh airport. Nothing reported in these weeks explains why more container ships made the passage.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The fight over the route's southern gate sharpened in October. Yemen's government said its forces took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on the way to Bab al-Mandeb, while Houthi missiles struck Riyadh's airport and an Aramco building in Dhahran. None of it accounts for the swings in canal transits.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The main Panama story was the 7.7 earthquake that toppled a tower in Penonomé and affected over 6,000 people. Nothing reported ties it, or any other event, to traffic through the canal.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was about Hormuz, not Malacca: Iran and Oman agreed a 'safe route', Saudi Arabia cut oil prices to Asia, then mines and strikes sank ships in the strait. Malacca carries that crude on to Asia, but nothing reported explains its own traffic.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The fortnight's reporting carried China's September export surge, led by chips, and BYD's move to own its car-carrier fleet as war raised freight costs, but none of it explains the late-August collapse and rebound in traffic through the strait.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was about Hormuz, where Iran's Guards claimed mine strikes on tankers and a container ship sank; none of it reaches traffic through Gibraltar or accounts for its swings.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh airport on successive days, one strike killing 13 and wounding over 300; by Monday 82% of flights were cancelled and Qatar Airways, Lufthansa and Air India had stopped flying. A missile then set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, as Yemen's government claimed Dhubab and the Mocha road near Bab al-Mandeb.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities. Its output decisions move the oil price, and its wars and alliances reach across the Gulf and the Red Sea.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi missiles struck Riyadh airport twice, killing 13 and wounding over 300, after earlier hits on airports in Jazan and Aden. Lufthansa, Air India and Qatar Airways halted flights. Under the Mecca Alliance, Pakistan and Turkey agreed to send troops, and the US backed Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: US prices rose 3.7% over the year in September, led by gasoline as the war's oil shock reached American pumps, and the figure set a 3.6% raise for 71 million Social Security beneficiaries. It capped a fortnight of tightening: India lifted its repo rate to 5.5%, and the ECB defended its hike with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Washington turned on Kyiv: Trump said Ukraine should elect a new president, and the US threatened to halt Europe-funded arms. Hungary then lifted its veto, opening 2 more EU accession clusters, Ukrainian drones hit 3 of Yandex's 6 Russian data centers, and SpaceX throttled Starlink terminals mid-mission.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at $1 if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2028. The price is a running bet on her standing against the rest of the party's field.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Iran's strikes in Hormuz this month hit shipping: 2 Emirati cargo ships sank, 6 ships were hit in one day with 2 Indian crew missing, and a US jet disabled an Iran-linked tanker. Trump dismissed intelligence that Russia and China help Iran. None of this accounts for the price.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: What traders pay for a contract that settles in full if David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. He is a free-market conservative in a crowded field on the French right.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its blockade of Iran before a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, and it moves with every sign of a deal or of escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran said Washington's reply to its proposal to reopen Hormuz met only some of its seven conditions, and the strait turned more violent after that: a US jet disabled an Iran-linked tanker, six ships were hit the next day with Indian crew missing, and two Emirati cargo ships sank within 24 hours.

stocks:UAL.standing: The parent of United Airlines, one of the three big US network carriers, with hubs including Chicago, Newark, Houston and San Francisco. Jet fuel is among its largest costs, so its shares move with oil prices and travel demand.

stocks:AXON.standing: The maker of the Taser and of the body cameras worn by most large American police forces, based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Its growth comes from the cloud subscriptions that store and manage the footage those cameras record.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat or stalled talk in the Gulf.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Iran's Guards spent the fortnight hitting ships in the Strait of Hormuz: six in one day, then 2 Emirati cargo ships sunk within 24 hours. Britain blamed them for the RAF Fairford plot. None of it was fire exchanged between Israel and Iran, and none of it accounts for the price.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: An IDC report put Nvidia at 34% of China's data-centre AI accelerator market in the first half of 2026, with Huawei at 28%: US export controls pushed Chinese buyers to domestic chips, and Nvidia's China shipments fell 44% to 678,000. A week earlier, SpaceX had placed a big Nvidia order.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home, a day before the share's high, entering a category Amazon is contesting with its own Alexa tablets. Earlier in the month it moved to restrict full disk access on the Mac for AI agents, after complaints over Meta Muse.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Gemini 4 Argon, announced after months of delays and first held back to trusted cyber defenders over safety concerns, launched globally on Oct 14 with its API price halved to $2 per million input tokens, though Google's own benchmarks put Claude ahead of it. A judge also dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits over AI Overviews.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's own news in the fortnight was about products and deals. It built its 1,000th satellite for Amazon Leo weeks ahead of the space Internet rollout, shuffled Alexa leadership after a new tablet, and may spend $7 billion on Decart, an AI startup Anthropic walked away from. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from its green card sponsorship scheme amid fraud claims, and its shares fell 7.5%. Days later the company set out a multi-gigawatt rollout of its own Maia AI accelerator racks for Azure, so more of its cloud runs on chips it designs. Separately, Norway fined its Xandr unit €8.5 million over Grindr data.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: Broadcom's own news this fortnight came from VMware, its software arm: a survey found licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options, and Topgolf said leaving saved it over $11.3 million. Neither accounts for the share's fall.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile sent Verizon and AT&T lower, while in India Starlink holds a licence but still cannot sell service. Then SpaceX throttled Ukraine's Starlink, dropping drone links at 110 km/h, and Musk blamed Washington for the Starshield limits.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta's Muse agent topped the US App Store within two weeks, and Meta says its new Muse model reaches the AI frontier after a 14-month push; Apple is tightening Mac privacy controls against AI agents after Muse complaints. Then a Frankfurt court held Meta liable for scam ads impersonating Finanzfluss, and Mexico gave it a month to protect minors.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on an oil facility near Riyadh as tankers were hit in Hormuz, and a missile later set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran. Aramco's chief executive said almost 3 billion barrels of supply had been lost and restocking could take two years, and Saudi Arabia unexpectedly cut its oil prices to Asia.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's sales fell 2 percent in Q3 2026, a result the trade press called underwhelming. A week later its entry into India stalled in acrimony, alongside Musk's Starlink, leaving the company without a growth market it had been courting.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung forecast a 780% jump in quarterly operating profit to 107.4 trillion won, a tech world first, on AI demand for its memory chips. Within days it and SK Hynix led South Korea's benchmark index down 5.5%, as doubts over AI spending and the rise of Chinese memory rivals hit both chipmakers at once.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: The peak came the day Micron said memory demand would exceed supply for at least 2 years, and its CEO said supplies were only getting tighter as AI data centres buy up chips. Nothing reported in the fortnight since accounts for the slide that followed.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: The fortnight's news about Eli Lilly was a trial testing a cousin of its obesity drug against alcohol use disorder, alongside Walmart's decision to cover some GLP-1s at no cost for its workers. Neither accounts for the share price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, along with Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, in a review spurred by worries over the banks' exposure to private credit, the lending that funds outside the banking system do and that banks increasingly finance.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK Hynix and Samsung dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% in a Seoul sell-off driven by doubts over AI spending and by the rise of Chinese memory rivals. Nothing in the input accounts for the earlier slide in the window.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one piece of news about Walmart's own business this fortnight was a staff benefit: it will offer 250-plus free medications to employees, covering some GLP-1s and insulin at no cost. Nothing in it accounts for the share's rise.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Results showed shipments to China up 109%, lifting its share of sales from 14% to 23%, while Washington presses the Netherlands to tighten export rules. A fourth-quarter forecast above expectations on AI chip demand came with them, but growth rests on the market US policy wants to close, so the share trades on Washington's next rule.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.
us-2y.recent: A Reuters piece on 2026-10-05 asked what Washington would do if US bond yields kept rising, but nothing in the input names the policy decision or data release behind the climb.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: The chart stops a month short of the newest figure: September's reading came in at 3.8%, the highest level in three years, and it kept pressure on the ECB to raise rates. Nothing published in the fortnight names what is pushing prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Solana's news this fortnight was engineering, not price: the network moved to halve its block times, set Oct. 21 for its Alpenglow upgrade targeting 150-millisecond finality, and the Solana Foundation launched DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds. None of it accounts for the token's swings.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The latest slide came as nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated alongside falls in bitcoin and ether. The ledger itself added controls for banks, stablecoins and tokenized funds, and the XRP Ledger Foundation explained a long-hidden bug that had threatened the 100 billion XRP cap.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.
doge.recent: Dogecoin gained an Ethereum-style testnet for trading, lending and stablecoins, and Bitcoin's soft-inflation pop faded as bond yields refused to fall. Neither accounts for the price over the window.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash's 25-second blocks went live on public testnet ahead of schedule, and nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. Neither explains the September swing in the price.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, and yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year earlier, as an oil shock routed through the Strait of Hormuz met a weak yen. Three sources told Reuters the Bank of Japan was ready to say underlying inflation had reached its 2% goal.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight's China finance news was about the currency, not the rate: Beijing rejected EU charges over the yuan as the bloc's deficit reached 360.6 billion euros, and the PBOC backed its FX policy. None of it concerns the lending rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The fortnight's news from the Bank of Russia was about the currency and not the cost of borrowing: international reserves fell 4.85% in September to $731.76 bln, the dollar was set at 83.25 rubles, and the bank made no yuan purchases or sales. None of it accounts for the rate.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The crude oil pumped from underground and refined into petrol, diesel, jet fuel and the feedstock for plastics. It is the world's most traded commodity, and its price runs through transport, food and inflation everywhere.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Attacks on tankers kept the region's crude bottled up: Kpler put Hormuz oil exports 42% below prewar levels, Iraq began trucking crude through Syria, and Kuwait pumps about 75% of its prewar oil. Aramco says almost 3 billion barrels of supply were lost and that replenishing it could take two years.

stocks:DAL.standing: One of the three largest US airlines, flying from hubs including Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis. Its share price moves on jet fuel costs and on demand for business and premium travel, and it reports results before its rivals.
stocks:DAL.recent: Delta cut its profit outlook after saying fuel will cost it $6 billion more this year, even with demand for seats holding strong. That is a squeeze on margins rather than on sales, and it arrived at the very end of the window, so it does not account for the share's earlier climb.

stocks:LLY.standing: An Indianapolis drugmaker whose tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company. Its share moves on demand, pricing and supply of that one drug class.
stocks:LLY.recent: The news about the company's own business was a push to take its obesity-drug cousin into alcohol use disorder, with trials also aimed at depression and schizophrenia. Walmart separately agreed to cover some GLP-1s at no cost for workers. Neither event accounts for the share price.

stocks:CSCO.standing: A San Jose maker of the routers, switches and security software that carry corporate and internet traffic. Its orders are read as a gauge of how much businesses and telecom carriers are spending on networks.
stocks:CSCO.recent: 10 countries signed trade deals with Washington that limit which telecom suppliers they may buy from. Terms like these decide who is allowed to sell network equipment in those markets, which is the business this company is in.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor by revenue and the maker of the F-35 fighter. Most of its sales come from the US government, so its share moves on Pentagon budgets and on foreign arms orders.
stocks:LMT.recent: Lockheed unveiled the PAC-3 Edge interceptor, which it says deploys from 2031, and the first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters ordered by Taiwan landed in Taipei. The IAF Chief said the US made no official offer to sell F-35 jets to India. None of it accounts for the share's fall.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The IMF and World Bank held their annual meetings in Bangkok this fortnight, where the IMF cut its Gulf forecasts over the prolonged Hormuz closure. None of that news concerned Thai listed companies or accounts for the index's path.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles struck Riyadh's airport, killing 13, and Lufthansa and Qatar Airways stopped flying to the capital. Then a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran after a Saudi-led coalition strike on Sanaa. The war had reached the oil company that dominates the index.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai's fortnight was taken up by the flydubai co-pilot plot, Iran's rejection of the US reply on reopening Hormuz, and inflation held above 5% by fuel costs. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's news from Manila was a survey finding 22.6% of families went involuntarily hungry in September, and a standoff in which the Philippines forced a Chinese survey ship away from Batanes. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta said its new Muse model reached the AI frontier after 14 months of rebuilding, and the Muse agent topped the US App Store within two weeks. A Frankfurt court held it liable for scam ads impersonating Finanzfluss. None of this dates to the late-September swing in the share.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, YouTube, Android and the Waymo robotaxi business. Most of its money comes from search advertising, so its share is a reading on the ad market and on whether AI erodes or extends search.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: A judge dismissed the antitrust suits Chegg and Penske brought against Google, and Google became the buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output. Its Gemini 4 Argon model went only to trusted cyber defenders, and its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of it. None of this lines up with the share's swings.

stocks:INFY.standing: India's second-largest IT services exporter, based in Bengaluru, selling software and outsourcing work to Western companies. Most of its revenue comes from North America, so US visa rules and tech budgets reach its share.
stocks:INFY.recent: The US suspended green-card sponsorship for 8 firms, including Infosys, which said it sees no material impact. The PERM programme governs whether a skilled foreign worker can stay permanently, not whether they can be billed to a client, so the firm's revenue is untouched while its engineers' path to residency stops.

stocks:WIT.standing: One of India's largest IT services firms, based in Bengaluru, selling outsourced software work and consulting to companies abroad. Most of its revenue comes from US and European clients, so their tech budgets and visa rules reach it.

stocks:TCS.NS.standing: India's largest IT services company, part of the Tata Group, running outsourced software and consulting for banks and corporations, mostly in North America and Europe. Its results gauge global corporate tech spending.
stocks:TCS.NS.recent: The shares rose on quarterly results: revenue grew 11% to ₹73,188 crore, driven by AI work and international business. TCS also built a higher bench and increased subcontracting as it prepares for demand, hiring ahead of contracts rather than after them.

stocks:CTSH.standing: An IT services and outsourcing firm based in New Jersey with most of its staff in India. It runs software for US banks, insurers and health companies, so its share moves on corporate tech budgets and US work-visa rules.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from US green-card sponsorship amid fraud claims that also caught Adobe, and the shares fell 7.5%. The climb back came as Microsoft said it would roll out its own Maia AI chips across Azure by the gigawatt, compute it designs rather than buys.

stocks:XPEV.standing: A Guangzhou-based maker of electric cars, listed in New York and Hong Kong. It designs its own driver-assistance software and chips, and sells into the most crowded and heavily discounted car market in the world.
stocks:XPEV.recent: XPENG branded its robotaxi business YOYO and on 8 October opened sign-ups in China by invitation code, a step beyond tests limited to its own employees but not a commercial launch. The car runs on four of the company's own Turing AI chips. The share's slide came before that announcement, and nothing reported accounts for it.

wiki-yemen.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on Yemen each day. The country sits on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the mouth of the Red Sea, so a war there reaches the shipping that runs between Europe and Asia.
wiki-yemen.recent: Yemen's government said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, with the Giants Brigades pushing toward Bab al-Mandeb. The Houthis answered by hitting Saudi airports: missiles on Riyadh's airport killed at least 3, and Lufthansa, Air India and Qatar Airways stopped flying there.

stocks:CMCSA.standing: The largest home broadband provider in the United States, and the owner of NBCUniversal, with the NBC network, Universal's film studio and theme parks, and Sky in Europe. Its earnings turn on households keeping a cable line.

stocks:DIS.standing: The share price of the entertainment group behind the Disney, Pixar and Marvel studios, the theme parks, Disney+, ABC and ESPN. The parks earn most of its profit, so it trades on household travel spending as much as on streaming.
stocks:DIS.recent: The one development in the input about Disney's own business is a report that Epic Games will let AI write all the code for its Disney shooter game, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

stocks:PSKY.standing: The owner of the CBS network, the Paramount film studio and the Paramount+ streaming service, controlled by the Ellison family. Its earnings turn on whether streaming grows faster than cable television shrinks.

stocks:FOXA.standing: The owner of Fox News, the Fox broadcast network, Fox Sports and the streaming service Tubi, controlled by the Murdoch family. Its income is cable fees and advertising sold against live news and sports.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The bet on a hold firmed after the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall that left the Fed seen skipping a hike. It gave ground when an inflation report raised rate-hike odds, though most Federal Reserve officials still expect another hike by year-end.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian and NATO forces clash directly before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with incidents on the alliance's border and with Ukraine talks.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The news from the war ran to truces rather than escalation: Washington hosted Ukraine and Europe in Miami without Russia, Kyiv paused refinery strikes for two days, and Germany and Ukraine pressed Putin to join a full energy-sector truce. Nothing in the fortnight put NATO forces in contact with Russian ones.

stocks:CVE.standing: A Calgary-based oil company and one of the largest producers in Canada's oil sands, with its own refineries in Canada and the United States. Its earnings turn on the discount heavy Canadian crude sells at against the US benchmark.
stocks:CVE.recent: Li Ka-shing's family sold a British grid for HK$110 billion and bought into Canadian oil sands, a swap that came after the share had already slid. Nothing in it accounts for the fall.

stocks:0001.HK.standing: A Hong Kong conglomerate built by Li Ka-shing, with ports, retail chains, telecoms networks and infrastructure across some 50 countries. Most of its earnings come from outside Hong Kong, so it trades on global trade and deal-making.
stocks:0001.HK.recent: Li Ka-shing's family sold a British grid for HK$110 billion, moving money out of regulated power networks. The sale was reported after the stretch the chart covers, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The one story about Tencent's own business was the retirement of its QClaw desktop agent, which shuts on 24 December. That came after the slide had already turned, and nothing in the input accounts for the share price.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: The trough came as Alibaba took the Pentagon to court, contesting its classification by the department and denying any link to the Chinese military. For a US-listed share, that designation reaches the holders themselves.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon's own news ran on several fronts: Amazon Leo built its 1,000th satellite and is weeks from a space Internet rollout, Alexa's leadership was reshuffled after a high-end tablet release, and Amazon may spend $7 billion on Decart, an AI startup Anthropic walked away from. None of it was tied to the share price.

stocks:EBAY.standing: An online marketplace where individuals and businesses sell new and used goods by auction or at a fixed price. It holds no stock itself and earns fees on each sale, so its revenue follows how much consumers spend through it.

stocks:AIR.PA.standing: Europe's largest aerospace company and one of the two builders of large passenger jets, with defence, helicopter and space arms. Its share moves on how many aircraft it delivers against a backlog that runs years ahead.
stocks:AIR.PA.recent: The fortnight's news about Airbus was all on the defence side: its U740 Valkyrie drone flew at Mach 0.8, Spain picked the A321 for a new electronic intelligence aircraft, and it detailed progress on the Lakota Connector uncrewed cargo helicopter. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
